 Advertisement Explore Betting on GOAL IMAGO Rian Rosendaal 40 minutes ago Last updated 17 Nov 2026, 16:17 Translated by Haaland fires Norway into Nations League quarter-finals in 96th minute
 Share Follow GOAL on Google Advertisement Norway have qualified for the Nations League quarter-finals as runners-up in Group D. They came from 2-0 down to beat Denmark 3-2 on Tuesday. Erling Haaland and his team-mates join group winners Portugal in the quarter-finals. 
 Haaland came close to opening the scoring after just six minutes, but Denmark goalkeeper Mads Hermansen denied the Norwegian superstar. The opening goal came at the other end instead: Rasmus Højlund scored from a rebound for the home side.
 Denmark soon went 2-0 up. Pierre-Emile Højbjerg headed home from close range to the delight of the Danish fans, leaving Norway with a much tougher task in Copenhagen.
 Haaland headed in, only for the VAR to rule out the goal for a handball shortly before it. Norway's hope returned when Hermansen let Martin Ødegaard dispossess him, leaving Haaland to tap in.
 Advertisement Advertisement Norway pushed hard to erase the deficit after the break. Antonio Nusa played Haaland in, but the striker shot just wide.

 After his earlier blunder, Hermansen made a fine save to deny Kristoffer Ajer with a quarter of an hour left. Time was running out for Norway, who needed a win to extend their Nations League campaign.
 Ødegaard scored from a rebound with seven minutes left, reviving Norway's hopes of reaching the quarter-finals. In the 96th minute, the VAR advised that Norway be awarded a penalty, and Haaland made it 3-2 at the death.
 Advertisement Norway join group winners Portugal in the Nations League quarter-finals. The draw takes place this Friday.
